title: PM2.5 next-hour prediction - Beijing, Aotizhongxin station (UCI)
summary: We predicted PM2.5 one hour ahead using the Beijing, Aotizhongxin station (UCI) data. XGBoost did best on the validation period, so we used it. On the test period (12 May 2016 to 28 Feb 2017) its average error was 9.693 µg/m³. Just repeating the last hour's value gave 10.338 µg/m³, so the model was 6.2% better. 165 episodes were flagged: 154 look like unusual pollution and 11 look like data problems.
how_it_was_made: Read the hourly data and treated empty cells and -200 as missing.

Built the inputs: hour, weekday, the reading 1 hour before, the reading 2 hours before, the reading 3 hours before, the reading at the same time the day before, temperature, air pressure, dew point, rain, wind speed.
Split the timeline in order: first 60% to train, next 20% to choose the model, last 20% to test.
Tried Linear Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost. Each predicts how much the level changes in the next hour.
Flagged test hours where the miss was more than 33.85 µg/m³ (bigger than 95% of the misses on the validation period).
Grouped flagged hours that were less than 3 hours apart and checked each group for missing data.
